info.name: Time-Off Microservice — Wizdaa Take-Home
info.description:
# Time-Off Microservice

A defensive time-off lifecycle service backed by NestJS + SQLite that syncs balances with an unreliable HCM source-of-truth over an at-least-once network. See `docs/TRD.md` for the full design (v3) and `docs/CONTRACTS.md` for the frozen interface spec.

## How to use this collection

1. Start the stack: `docker compose up --build` (app on `:3000`, mock HCM on `:3001`).
2. Seed the mock HCM with a starting balance — **Mock HCM Controls → Refresh HCM balance** (default seeds `emp1/loc1 → 20` days).
3. Walk through **Guided Scenarios** in order — each one references requests from folders 1–5.

## Auth model

This service assumes an upstream gateway has authenticated the caller and injected:

- `X-Employee-Id` — the principal's employee ID (trusted)
- `X-Role` — `employee` or `manager`

The collection variables `employee_id`, `manager_id`, and `role` are wired into every header by default. Switch `role` to `manager` for manager-only routes (approve, reject, resolve-review).

## Idempotency

`POST /time-off-requests` requires an `Idempotency-Key` header (UUID). The collection pre-request script generates a fresh one for each submit. Replay the same submit with the same key to verify idempotent behavior (ADR-012).

## State machine cheat-sheet

```
DRAFT ─submit─► PENDING ─approve─► PENDING_SYNC ─FILE ack─► APPROVED
                  │                     │ └─retry cap─► REVERSE ► REJECTED
                  │                     └─cancel─► CANCELLED (+ REVERSE if FILE sent)
                  ├─reject───────────► REJECTED
                  └─TTL (reaper)─────► EXPIRED
APPROVED ─cancel─► CANCELLED (+ REVERSE)
```

Under the **Pure Outbox** model (ADR-013), `approve` always lands in `PENDING_SYNC` first; the dispatcher promotes to `APPROVED` on the FILE ack from HCM.

item.name: 1. Setup & Health
item.description: Sanity checks before walking through scenarios. Use these to confirm both services are up and reachable.

request.description: Returns `{ status: 'ok' }` when the app is up. Used by the Docker healthcheck.
Returns the batch corpus the mock HCM would emit next. Doubles as a liveness probe for the mock — also used by its Docker healthcheck.

item.name: 2. Employee Workflow
item.description: All requests here use `X-Role: employee` and `X-Employee-Id: {{employee_id}}`. An employee may only act on their **own** records — IDOR is enforced server-side (§12).

request.description:
Returns the current `Balance` row for `(employee_id, location_id)`. Creates a zero record on first access. Response fields: `available`, `reserved`, `needsReview`, `lastHcmAsOf`, `version`.

Under Model A: `available` mirrors HCM's free-days view; `reserved` = days held by PENDING requests.

exec: // Generate a fresh Idempotency-Key for each submit (ADR-012).
// Re-running the SAME request without changing the key will replay (E8).
// Override by setting `idempotency_key` in collection variables to test replay.

request.description:
Submit a time-off request (ADR-012). The server computes `days` from the inclusive date range, excluding weekends (location calendar is stubbed for v1 per A6).

**Headers**
- `X-Employee-Id` — must match the body's `employeeId` (IDOR check, §12)
- `X-Role: employee`
- `Idempotency-Key` — UUID; replays return the SAME request if active (E8); 422 on key reuse with a different body (E23)

**Body**
- `employeeId`, `locationId`, `startDate` (YYYY-MM-DD inclusive), `endDate` (YYYY-MM-DD inclusive)
- **No `days` field** — server-computed (§12)

**Responses**
- `201` — request created in `PENDING`, `reserved += days` on the balance
- `409` — insufficient balance OR overlap with an existing active request (E1, E19, E20)
- `422` — idempotency-key reuse with a different body (E23)

The test script captures the new request `id` into `request_id` for subsequent approve/reject/cancel calls.

Cancel the captured request (`request_id`). Behavior depends on current status:

- **PENDING** → void pending FILE outbox + `release` (reserved -= days) → `CANCELLED`
- **PENDING_SYNC** (FILE not sent) → void FILE + `restore` (available += days) → `CANCELLED`
- **PENDING_SYNC** (FILE already SENT) → `restore` + enqueue REVERSE → `CANCELLED` (E27)
- **APPROVED** → `restore` + enqueue REVERSE → `CANCELLED` (E9, FR-6)
- already **CANCELLED** → no-op (idempotent)

A manager can cancel any request; an employee can only cancel their own (IDOR).

item.name: 3. Manager Workflow
item.description: Manager-only routes: approve, reject, resolve-review. All use `X-Role: manager`. The `X-Employee-Id` header here is the **manager's** ID — IDOR for the target employee is handled inside the service.

request.description:
Approve a PENDING request (ADR-001).

**Approve sequence** under the **Pure Outbox** model (ADR-013):
1. GET HCM realtime balance (best-effort; if HCM is unreachable → proceed on local cache per ADR-001).
2. `applyHcmSnapshot` — set local `available = hcmValue`.
3. Re-validate locally: if `available < days` → REJECTED + `release` (E10).
4. Past-date check — if `startDate < now` (location-tz civil date) → REJECTED + `release` (E18).
5. In one transaction: `commit` (available -= days, reserved -= days), write `Outbox(FILE, PENDING)`, status → **PENDING_SYNC**.

The dispatcher promotes `PENDING_SYNC → APPROVED` once HCM acks the FILE (E4 happy). On retry-cap, the dispatcher fires the compensating REVERSE path (E5).

exec: // Happy path under Pure Outbox: approve always lands in PENDING_SYNC;
// dispatcher (5s @Interval) promotes to APPROVED on FILE ack.

request.description:
Reject a PENDING or PENDING_SYNC request.

- **PENDING** → `release` (reserved -= days) → REJECTED
- **PENDING_SYNC** → void pending FILE + `restore` (available += days, the commit is undone) → REJECTED

`reason` is accepted but not persisted in v1 (extensibility seam).

Clear `Balance.needsReview` on a flagged balance (B4 / ADR-003).

When reconciliation drives `available` negative, the balance is flagged with `needsReview=true` and a `FLAGGED_NEGATIVE` event is emitted (E26). After the manager investigates and accepts the divergence (or manually adjusts), they call this endpoint to clear the flag.

Manager-only. This is the ONE BalanceService method that acquires the per-balance-key lock itself.

item.name: 4. HCM Batch Sync
item.description: The HCM → service push (§8). HCM emits a full balance corpus periodically (or on events like year-start); the service reconciles each balance against the snapshot under ADR-003's algorithm.

request.description:
Ingest a batch corpus from HCM (ADR-009 + ADR-003).

**Sequence guard (ADR-009):** `sequence` must be strictly greater than the last applied sequence. A stale or out-of-order batch is rejected and audited with a single `STALE_REJECTED` reconciliation event (E13).

**Per-balance reconcile (ADR-003):** for each entry, under the per-balance-key lock:
- base `available = entry.balance`
- subtract days for any `APPROVED` or `PENDING_SYNC` request whose `hcmAckAt` is NULL or > `asOf` (snapshot misses these)
- add days for any pending REVERSE outbox row whose linked request is `CANCELLED`
- `reserved` recomputed from current `PENDING` requests only
- if final `available < 0` → set `needsReview = true` + emit `FLAGGED_NEGATIVE` (E26)

In production this endpoint would require a service token. In v1 it's open by design (commented in the controller).

**Bump `sequence` between runs!** The service rejects any sequence ≤ the last applied one.

item.name: 5. Mock HCM Controls
item.description:
Test-control surface on the mock HCM (`:3001`). These endpoints exist ONLY in the mock — in a real deployment the `mock-hcm` service is dropped and the real HCM has no `_control/*` routes (§12).

Use these to:
- Set HCM-side starting balance (`/_control/refresh`)
- Switch behavior between scenarios (`/_control/scenario`)
- Preview or emit a batch corpus (`/_control/batch`, `/_control/emit-batch`)
- Directly inspect HCM-side state (`GET /hcm/balance`)

request.description:
Overwrite an HCM-side balance with a new value (and refresh `asOf` to now). Simulates a year-start refresh or work-anniversary bonus, making E7 / E10 / E26 scenarios deterministic.

Run this once at the start of a session to seed a known balance, e.g. `{ balance: 20 }`.

Switch the mock's behavior. ADR-007 scenarios:

| Scenario | Effect |
|---|---|
| `correct` | Normal semantics; idempotency dedup applies. |
| `silent-insufficient` | `POST /hcm/timeoff` returns 200 even on insufficient balance, WITHOUT deducting (E3). |
| `timeout` | All `/hcm/*` calls fail (503) — exercises the dispatcher retry / retry-cap path. |
| `mutate-between-calls` | Each `GET /hcm/balance` decrements by 1 — exercises E10. |
| `divergent-batch` | Batch corpus reports each balance 3 below the real value (E6). |
| `duplicate-delivery` | Behaves like `correct` (idempotency-key dedup still holds; E11/E16). |
| `ignore-idempotency-key` | Skips dedup table — proves the service's local guard holds even when HCM ignores ADR-008. |
Return the corpus the mock WOULD emit next. Non-destructive (does NOT advance the sequence counter). Useful for inspecting state before triggering a real ingest.

Build a fresh corpus (advancing the sequence counter) and POST it to `targetUrl`. The default uses the Docker network hostname `app:3000` — if you're calling Postman from outside Docker, swap it for `http://host.docker.internal:3000` or `http://localhost:3000` depending on how your Docker daemon resolves the host.

Optional overrides: `balances`, `asOf`, `sequence`.

Inspect the HCM-side balance directly (debugging / cross-checking). The service never calls this from Postman — the HcmClient does — but it's useful to verify HCM-side state after a FILE or REVERSE has landed.

item.name: 6. Guided Scenarios
item.description:
Walkthroughs that exercise key E-matrix flows end-to-end. Each scenario lists the requests to run in order and what to verify at each step. Folders 1–5 hold the actual reusable requests — these notes glue them together.

Reset between scenarios by running **Mock HCM Controls → Seed / refresh HCM balance** with your starting value, and the **DELETE volumes** Docker step if you want a fresh DB (`docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d`).

request.description:
## A — Happy path

Demonstrates the canonical lifecycle through the Pure Outbox dispatcher.

1. **Setup → Mock HCM Controls → Seed / refresh HCM balance** with `balance: 20`.
2. **Employee Workflow → View own balance** — expect `available=0, reserved=0` (first read auto-creates a zero row).
3. **Mock HCM Controls → Set scenario** with `correct`.
4. **Employee Workflow → Submit time-off** — request lands `PENDING`, `reserved=2`.
5. **Employee Workflow → View own balance** — expect `available=0, reserved=2`.
6. **Manager Workflow → Approve request** — server commits locally, writes outbox FILE, status → **PENDING_SYNC**. The collection's test script accepts PENDING_SYNC or APPROVED depending on dispatcher timing.
7. Wait ~5s (or run multiple GETs) for the dispatcher's `@Interval(5000)` to fire — it sends the FILE to mock HCM and promotes status to **APPROVED**.
8. **Employee Workflow → View own balance** — expect `available` dropped by 2 (Model A: commit reduced available).
9. **Mock HCM Controls → Direct: get HCM balance** — expect HCM-side balance is 18 (the FILE landed and deducted).

The `GET /` body of this request is a placeholder so Postman lets you click 'Send' on a guide; the real action is in the description above.

## B — E1 Insufficient at submit

1. **Mock HCM → Refresh** with `balance: 2` (small).
2. **Mock HCM → Set scenario** `correct`.
3. Edit **Submit time-off** to span a long range (e.g. `startDate: 2026-06-01`, `endDate: 2026-06-30` → ~22 business days).
4. **Submit** — expect **409 Conflict** with a message about `available − reserved < days`.
5. **View balance** — no reservation occurred (balance unchanged).

The local guard (`available − reserved < days`) rejects before any HCM call. ADR-001 / E1.

## C — E8 Idempotent replay

1. **Mock HCM → Refresh** with `balance: 20`.
2. Set collection variable `reuse_idempotency_key = true` (forces the pre-request script to reuse the existing `idempotency_key`).
3. **Submit time-off** — captures `request_id` and an `idempotency_key`.
4. **Submit** again WITHOUT changing the body — expect the SAME `id` is returned. `reserved` did NOT double.
5. Now change the date range in the body and **Submit** again with the same key — expect **422 Unprocessable** (key-reuse-with-different-body, E23).
6. Set `reuse_idempotency_key = false` to restore fresh-UUID behavior.

## D — E20 Boundary-touching ranges collide

1. **Refresh** balance to 20; scenario `correct`.
2. **Submit** `startDate=2026-06-02, endDate=2026-06-03`. Expect PENDING.
3. Set `reuse_idempotency_key = false` (so a NEW key is generated).
4. **Submit** with the same `{{employee_id}}/{{location_id}}` but `startDate=2026-06-03, endDate=2026-06-04`. Expect **409 Conflict** — the inclusive overlap predicate catches the shared June 3.

ADR-012 ②. Boundary-touching ranges are rejected, not silently trimmed.

## E — E9 Cancel approved

1. Walk through scenario **A** so a request reaches `APPROVED` and HCM-side balance is debited (e.g. 18).
2. **Employee Workflow → Cancel** the captured `request_id`. Status → `CANCELLED`. `available += days`. A REVERSE outbox row is enqueued with key `{hcmIdempotencyKey}:REVERSE`.
3. Wait ~5s for the dispatcher to send the REVERSE.
4. **Mock HCM → Direct: get HCM balance** — expect balance back at 20 (REVERSE credited the days back at HCM).

Idempotency: the REVERSE key is suffixed, so HCM cannot conflate it with the FILE.

## F — E7 Anniversary bonus via batch

1. **Refresh** HCM with `balance: 30` (bonus added).
2. **HCM Batch Sync → Ingest** with `sequence` greater than any previously sent (use `2`, `3`, … as you experiment) and `balances[].balance = 30`.
3. **View own balance** — expect `available = 30` minus any local unacked deductions. Pending requests intact in `reserved`.

ADR-003 + ADR-009. PENDING reservations are NOT subtracted from the HCM base because HCM doesn't know about them; they only affect `reserved`.

## G — E4 HCM timeout at approve

1. **Refresh** HCM balance to 20.
2. **Mock HCM → Set scenario** `timeout`.
3. **Submit** (lands PENDING).
4. **Approve** — status → **PENDING_SYNC**, the outbox FILE row is `PENDING`. Local balance committed (available -= days).
5. Wait — the dispatcher tries every 5s. Each retry fails (`hcm.callsTo.fileTimeOff` increments in the mock). After `HCM_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (5) failures, the **retry-cap compensation path** fires:
   - outbox FILE → `FAILED`
   - `restore` (available += days)
   - status → `REJECTED`
   - new REVERSE outbox row enqueued
6. **Set scenario** back to `correct`. The REVERSE outbox row gets sent next tick → idempotent no-op at HCM (no FILE landed).

ADR-004 / E5. The whole flow is non-blocking from the user's perspective.

## H — E26 Year-start drop → needsReview

1. Walk through **A** so a request is APPROVED locally (`available = 18`).
2. **Refresh** HCM with `balance: 2` (simulating a year-start drop AFTER the local approval).
3. **Ingest batch** with the new `balance: 2` and `sequence` greater than the last.
4. The reconcile algorithm computes `2 − 2 (unacked APPROVED) = 0` — or negative if the local commit hadn't acked yet. If negative, `needsReview = true` and a `FLAGGED_NEGATIVE` event is emitted.
5. **View own balance** — observe `needsReview: true`.
6. **Manager → Resolve review** — clears the flag.

B4 / ADR-003. The system never silently goes negative; a human must adjudicate.

## I — E15 Reaper reclaims stale reservation

The reaper runs every 5 minutes (`@Cron(EVERY_5_MINUTES)`) and reservation TTL is 14 days by default (`RESERVATION_TTL_DAYS`).

To test in real time you'd either wait (impractical) or lower the TTL via env: stop the stack with `docker compose down`, edit `compose.yml`'s `RESERVATION_TTL_DAYS: 0` (or a small fractional day requires code change), and bring it back up.

For a meaningful demo, the **E15 test in `src/__tests__/cancel-and-reaper.spec.ts`** is the deterministic version — it injects a `FakeClock`, advances it 15 days, calls `reaper.sweep()` directly, and asserts the request → `EXPIRED` + reservation released + outbox FILE voided. See it in action via `npm run test`.

The Postman flow is mostly for awareness — the unit/integration test is the rigorous verification.

When true, Submit's pre-request script keeps the existing idempotency_key instead of minting a fresh one.
